item.title: West Bank: Palestinians harvest olives under Israeli military restrictions
item.description: Palestinian farmers in the occupied West Bank have been allowed limited access to their olive groves under Israeli military restrictions. Many found damaged trees, while soldiers fired tear gas near the harvest.

item.title: Spain: Zelensky urges Latin America to help repair Ukraine's power grid
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has appealed to Spain and Latin American countries for urgent help repairing Ukraine's damaged energy infrastructure. He also met King Felipe VI during the Ibero-American Summit in Madrid.

item.title: Paraguayan president resigns amid bank collapse leaving 3M people without access to bank accounts
item.description: Santiago Peña resigned as president of Paraguay amid the Ueno Bank crisis and was later impeached over an alleged conflict of interest. Vice President Pedro Alliana will take office, while millions of Paraguayans wait to recover their deposits.

item.title: British comedian Russell Brand found guilty of rape and three sexual assaults by London jury
item.description: Russell Brand was convicted of four sexual offences, one rape and three sexual assaults, involving four women between 2005 and 2009 in different locations.

item.title: Greece: Students march in Athens demanding more education funding
item.description: Thousands of pupils, students and teachers marched through central Athens on Thursday in a nationwide push for better-funded schools, joining a protest wave that has spread from France across southern Europe.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 5th, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 5th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: World Investment Forum in Doha examines what attracts investment and what holds it back
item.description: Foreign investment remains concentrated in relatively few countries, while others struggle to attract funding. At the World Investment Forum in Doha, governments and businesses discussed how more economies could benefit and turn investment into jobs.

item.title: Putin seizes Russian operations of cigarette giant Japan Tobacco International
item.description: The decree transferred JTI’s four factories, around 4,000 employees and roughly 40% of the Russian cigarette market to a state-linked holding company. The latest seizure added to a list that includes Nestlé, Auchan, Leroy Merlin and Metro.

item.title: Everyday people: Jeans, plastic and paper among Met Gala's surprising new fashion themes
item.description: The 2027 Met Gala will celebrate the potential of everyday objects and materials, from jeans and T-shirts to paper and plastic. The accompanying exhibition next spring will explore how designers transform ordinary items into works of art.

item.title: EU plans to deliver 'AI literacy' certificates to students
item.description: The European Union has announced that it has started to work on creating a certificate for "AI literacy" that would be delivered to successful 15-year-old students for the next school year.

item.title: Italian PM slams EU’s fragmented approach to Ukraine peace talks
item.description: In a letter to European Council President António Costa, Giorgia Meloni says multiple negotiating formats are making Europe “less credible” to end the war.

item.title: Protesters across Europe to call for freeze on energy hungry data centres
item.description: After US midterms, European campaigners bring the data centre backlash to Europe.

item.title: Fireworks may be fun, but their health risks are not
item.description: Fireworks may be a staple of celebrations, but their health risks are prompting experts to call for stricter regulations and greater public awareness.

item.title: Ueno Bank collapse in Paraguay prompts President Santiago Peña to resign
item.description: The accounting black hole at Ueno Bank wipes out public funds, leaves thousands without access to their deposits and drives Paraguay into its worst institutional crisis in years.

item.title: France: Up to 55,000 march in Lyon amid clashes and tear gas
item.description: Tens of thousands marched through Lyon area during a nationwide strike over wages and purchasing power. Police charged demonstrators and used tear gas as clashes erupted along the protest route.

item.title: More flights, fewer emissions: this country’s aviation challenge
item.description: Azerbaijan is working to reduce aviation emissions while handling growing air traffic. From fuel-efficient aircraft and airport carbon accreditation to digital air navigation, the industry is exploring ways to make flying more sustainable.

item.title: Inside New Tashkent, Uzbekistan's planned city for two million people
item.description: Nearly 7,000 apartments are complete, three ministries already operate there and university facilities have opened. Projects worth $50bn (€44.8bn) are planned for the first phase, with a FIFA-standard stadium under construction and a metro connection proposed.

item.title: Bank of England raises key interest rate for first time in over 3 years
item.description: The Bank of England has raised interest rates to 4% as it tries to curb rising prices fuelled by the Iran war.

item.title: South Korea plans to extend anti-piracy patrols closer to Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Seoul said pirates have recently ventured further from the Somali coast and added that it wanted to send a patrol aircraft to protect merchant ships off Oman while keeping its forces out of the ongoing Iran war.

item.title: Uzbekistan's poverty rate falls as World Bank highlights role of wages and employment
item.description: The Bank estimates that the national rate fell from 17% in 2021 to 5.8% in 2025, with 3.7 million people moving above the threshold. The government separately reports 3.6% for the first nine months of 2026.

item.title: Milei and Sánchez exchange a cold greeting at Ibero-American Summit
item.description: Argentine President Javier Milei and Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez exchanged a brief and frosty greeting at the Ibero-American Summit in Madrid on Wednesday. Their encounter comes two weeks after Milei called Sánchez an “unpresentable dictator”.

item.title: France: Mass protests and school blockades mark fourth national strike
item.description: Hundreds of thousands joined a fourth nationwide day of protests across France. Police used tear gas outside a Paris school, while major demonstrations disrupted Marseille and Nantes.

item.title: EU Commission holds first talks with Serbia’s Student List
item.description: EU Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos met four Student List representatives in Brussels on Monday, the party’s first high-level EU contact since its landslide win. Talks centred on democracy and domestic affairs, as polling irregularities delay the new government.

item.title: China threatens EU with retaliation as EU mulls “kill-switch” to defend its market
item.description: Despite ongoing talks to rebalance EU-China trade, Brussels is preparing a powerful new tool to shield its market from a surge of cheap Chinese imports.

item.title: Leonardo tops €60 billion in orders as defence, drones and space grow
item.description: Leonardo recorded a 28% increase in orders in the first nine months of 2026. The Italian group is focusing on defence, aerospace, drones and new industrial partnerships, while the acquisition of Iveco Group's Defence division has strengthened its position.

item.title: Poland arrests six suspected of spying for Russia and supplying its military
item.description: The charges against the group of six also include violations of regulations governing the international trade in goods and technologies of strategic importance for national defence and international security.

item.title: Portugal great Cristiano Ronaldo announces retirement from international football
item.description: "To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the No. 7 shirt of our national team,” the 41-year-old Ronaldo said in a long video message on social media.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 5th, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 5th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: North Korea tells EU to 'mind its own business' after draft UN resolution on human rights
item.description: The United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights said last year that human rights in North Korea have shown no improvement over the past decade and had in fact worsened in many cases.

item.title: Iran: Flames engulf banner depicting US and Israeli leaders
item.description: Demonstrators in Tehran burned a banner depicting US and Israeli leaders during rallies marking the 1979 US embassy takeover. The protests followed a major electoral setback for Donald Trump.

item.title: Rheinmetall shares plunge more than 17% after profit warning over order delays
item.description: German defence giant Rheinmetall warned of delays to military contracts and ammunition approvals, sending its shares down more than 17% in early trading on Thursday.

item.title: Europe is betting €525 million on chip design start-ups
item.description: A new initiative under the EU's Chips Act targets a segment where European firms account for less than 1% of global revenues.

item.title: Drone strike sets Ozon warehouse ablaze in southern Russia
item.description: A fire broke out at an Ozon warehouse in Adygeysk, southern Russia, on Wednesday. The Russian e-commerce giant said the facility had been targeted in a drone attack.

item.title: ABB enters Uzbekistan, bringing Azerbaijan’s digital banking expertise to a new market in Asia
item.description: ABB is expanding into Uzbekistan through the acquisition of Davr Bank, as regional financial institutions accelerate digital banking growth across Central Asia and emerging markets.

item.title: Finnish court jails Russian captain over Baltic Sea cable sabotage
item.description: The Russian captain was ordered jailed for three years and six months and the crew member, an Azerbaijan national, for two years and 10 months.

item.title: Ukraine: Russian drone and missile attack sparks fire in Kyiv region
item.description: A Russian strike on a logistics facility in Sofiivska Borshchahivka, in the Kyiv region, injured one man and sparked a major fire, with emergency crews battling the flames following an overnight attack involving 128 drones and two missiles.

item.title: Russia plans ticket surcharge to bankroll struggling aircraft industry
item.description: From 2027, passengers would pay 500 roubles on domestic flights and 1,000 on international flights to fund the lease and operation of 258 Russian-built aircraft, as sactions over Moscow's all-out war in Ukraine continue to bite.

item.title: Hundreds of thousands march in nationwide strike in France as government backs austerity budget
item.description: Hundreds of thousands of protestors demonstrated across France on Thursday, a day after French lawmakers rejected the first part of the 2027 budget bill, in a unified consensus across party lines.

item.title: 'Too early' to say if Europe flight bomb threats linked, EU transport chief says
item.description: The incidents come after some 27 European flights were targeted by bomb threats on Tuesday, forcing the brief closure of a Warsaw airport and the scrambling of air force planes in Rome.

item.title: ‘It would destroy the Democrat Party’: Trump dismisses impeachment threat
item.description: US President Donald Trump has warned that impeaching him would damage the Democratic Party, after Republicans suffered major losses in the midterm elections.

item.title: NASA astronauts cast US election votes from the International Space Station
item.description: In a rare event, three American astronauts voted in Tuesday's US midterm elections from the International Space Station, using advanced links to send electronic ballots to officials on Earth.

item.title: 'Cautious optimism' for renewed US engagement on climate as delegation heads to COP31
item.description: Delegation members plan to "explore opportunities for renewed US engagement on climate, energy, and economic policy" at the UN summit.

item.title: Americans 'stay optimists', 'tremendous growth' in AI to continue, says US-EU wealth manager Xavier Volatier
item.description: Xavier Volatier, head of Transatlantic Private Wealth, speaks to our Stefan Grobe on the effects of the US mid-terms' result on the global markets.

item.title: Tearful reunions as Ukrainians return from Russian-occupied Oleshky
item.description: Residents of Russian-occupied Oleshky have arrived back in Ukrainian-controlled territory, reuniting with relatives after enduring worsening living conditions.

item.title: Supermarket freezer cyberattack 'not sophisticated,' Prof. Kevin Curran explains
item.description: Stefan Grobe speaks to Kevin Curran, Professor of Cybersecurity at the University of Ulster. He explains that the attack was 'not sophisticated', and vulnerabilities were known long term.

item.title: Change in Texas could 'shape the US presidential election', says analyst Eric Ham
item.description: Eric Ham, US political analyst, said that US Democrats believe that many African-American, Latino and young voters are again "up for grabs" after they gave their support for Trump in past presidential elections.

item.title: Gaza: Displaced Palestinian builds wind turbine to generate electricity
item.description: A displaced Palestinian in Gaza has built a makeshift wind turbine to bring electricity to tents in Khan Younis. Unable to afford solar panels, he has found a way to harness the wind to power everyday essentials.

item.title: Oil giants cash in on the US-Iran conflict. Can an EU-wide tax on oil profits ease the energy crisis?
item.description: A new report commissioned by Greenpeace Germany found that oil companies earned €36 billion in additional margins from the fallout of the US-Iran conflict between March 1 and October 19. Can Europe tax these profits to help ease rising energy bills?

item.title: Iran is a 'wounded animal' and will 'seek revenge', Pahlavi says
item.description: Reza Pahlavi, son of the former Shah of Iran, thinks the Iranian regime is "willing to go all the way for its own survival".

item.title: What Macron really said: Private Telegram exchanges revealed in new book
item.description: Françoise Degois publishes "You are all too hard on me", a book in which she records her private exchanges with the president.
